trap-nonspeakable.notes: RIGOR (reported, not fixed - MAJOR, two of the three rigidity inputs are false as stated on the block's own branch; verified numerically at 30 dps from the block's own product formula, b = sqrt(t/2pi) e^{i pi/4}, t = ln q0 = 0.1043407203, |b| = 0.1288655943, b^2 = 0.0166063414i so Im b^2 > 0 as required). (1) ITEM 1 IS WRONG. The block writes 'The inversion relation Phi_b(x)Phi_b(-x) = c_0'. Computed from the block's own products, Phi_b(z)Phi_b(-z) is NOT constant: (6.7171e6 + 1.9515e6 i) at z = 0.3, (2.1971e5 + 6.9913e6 i) at z = 0.7, (-5.5270e6 - 4.2872e6 i) at z = 1.1. Dividing by e^{i pi z^2} gives 6994799.44082 at ALL THREE points to 12 digits. So the correct relation is Phi_b(z)Phi_b(-z) = c_0 . e^{i pi z^2} - Faddeev's Gaussian inversion relation - not a constant. (The Gaussian cancels in the ratio Phi_1/Phi_b if both solutions satisfy it, so the CONCLUSION of item 1 may survive; the stated relation does not.) (2) ITEM 2 IS WRONG ON THIS BRANCH. 'sigma-unitarity (self-duality, |Phi_b| = 1)' fails badly: |Phi_b(0)| = 2644.768315, |Phi_b(0.3)| = 8243.118301, |Phi_b(-0.3)| = 848.562302, |Phi_b(1.1)| = 142623.4128. Unitarity of Faddeev's Phi_b requires b real or |b| = 1 (b^2 real); the physical branch chosen here has b^2 PURELY IMAGINARY, which is exactly what makes the products converge (|e^{i pi b^2}| = 0.9491671528, |e^{-i pi/b^2}| = 6.9e-83) and exactly what destroys unitarity. Proposed: either restate items 1-2 with the Gaussian factor and a unitarity condition that holds on Im b^2 > 0, or state the rigidity argument on the branch where unitarity is available and transfer by analytic continuation. (3) VERIFIED CORRECT: the branch condition Im b^2 > 0 does hold for the stated physical b, and both infinite products converge there; the product written is Faddeev's Phi_b in the standard (-q e^{2 pi b z}; q^2)_inf / (-q~^{-1} e^{2 pi z/b}; q~^{-2})_inf normalisation.
